questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -3 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{12\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 0+9\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{12\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 1+9\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 2 \\ 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-2)\cdot (-3)+(-2)\cdot 2+(-9)\cdot 1}{(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-2)\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 2+(-9)\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}w=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot 2+5\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{(-3)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 1+5\cdot 0+1\cdot 2}{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot 0+5\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x$ or any other non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ 

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}\,x}{‖x‖\,‖{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x‖} \\  & =\frac{(-3)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 3}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{18}{\sqrt{36}\sqrt{18}} \\  & =\frac{18}{6\cdot 3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
